analysis.evidence: וְאֶת marks הַחֹרִי as another object of the preceding verb of striking. The plural suffix in בְּהַרְרָם, “in their hill country,” identifies the Horites collectively as the people living in Seir.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute gentilic used as a noun. The singular refers collectively to the people.

analysis.evidence: שֵׂעִיר names the Horites’ hill country, and עַד אֵיל פָּארָן traces the campaign as far as El-paran. The geographic setting supports the regional sense of הַר.
analysis.morphology: The locative preposition בְּ precedes a masculine singular construct noun with a third-person masculine plural possessive suffix referring to the Horites.

analysis.evidence: In עַד אֵיל פָּארָן, עַד introduces El-paran as the geographic limit reached in the campaign against the Horites.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: as far as, up to, to (a place or person)

analysis.evidence: עַד אֵיל פָּארָן marks the endpoint of the route, “as far as the terebinth of Paran.” The clause אֲשֶׁר עַל הַמִּדְבָּר locates that landmark at the edge of the wilderness. The source’s proper-name tag fits the full place-name אֵיל פָּארָן, while the marked word supplies its tree element.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state. אֵיל is the construct form of אַיִל, with פָּארָן as its complement.
analysis.sense: A great tree or terebinth that gives a location its name.
